chunks: It means that the believers follow me, while the wicked follow wealth, just as the bees follow their 'ya'sūb' (leader), who is their chief.

key_terms.فُجَّارَ: The wicked or ungodly, those who lack piety and are driven by base desires.
key_terms.يَعْسُوبُ: The queen bee or leader of the bee colony, used here as a metaphor for the object of leadership or devotion.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between how believers and the wicked are led, according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi employs the metaphor of the bee colony's queen (ya'sūb) to distinguish between the conscious, spiritual obedience of the faithful and the instinctual, materialistic drive of the wicked. This commentary highlights the theological contrast in Nahj al-Balagha between divine guidance and worldly attachment, framing leadership as a natural order akin to biological instinct. The analogy underscores that while believers follow reason and revelation, the fujjar are governed by the primal pull of wealth.

en.sayed-ali-raza: It means that the believers follow me while the wicked follow wealth just as the bees follow their “ya‘sūb” who is their leader. [1]
